title: CommutAir flight 4821
summary: A Beechcraft 1900C conducting an ILS approach to Adirondack Regional Airport descended below the glide slope near Gabriels, New York. title: Air Inter 148

agencies.name: Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety

summary: Air Inter Flight 148 crashed into Mont Sainte-Odile in the Vosges Mountains while approaching Strasbourg Airport. The pilots set the autopilot to Vertical Speed Mode instead of Flight Path Angle Mode, then entered a descent rate of 3300 feet per minute instead of the intended 3.3 degrees. The ambiguous autopilot display showed only two digits, masking the actual high descent rate. The aircraft lacked a ground proximity warning system that might have alerted the crew.

title: USAir 405
summary: USAir Flight 405, a Fokker F28, was attempting to take off from LaGuardia Airport in poor weather conditions on March 22, 1992. Due to inadequate ground de-icing procedures at LaGuardia and weather-related delays up to 35 minutes, a significant accumulation of ice formed on the wings and airframe. The flight crew was unaware of the extent of ice buildup. The aircraft lifted off but failed to gain altitude, flying only several meters above the ground. The aircraft veered off the runway and struck several obstructions before coming to rest in Flushing Bay. Of the 51 people on board, 27 were killed, including the captain and one cabin crew member.
probable_cause: Ice accumulated on the wings and airframe due to inadequate de-icing procedures and weather delays, increasing drag and reducing lift. The aircraft attempted rotation at too low an airspeed, preventing the achievement of flight. Insufficient deicing procedures at LaGuardia, compounded by the crew's unawareness of ice extent, contributed to the accident.

title: Copa Airlines 201
summary: A 12-year-old Boeing 737-200 experienced a faulty wiring harness in the Attitude Director Indicator system that caused intermittent false data. The pilots switched both ADI displays to receive data from the same faulty gyro, creating a feedback loop where the aircraft appeared to be banking left when it was actually rolling right. This led to an uncontrolled 80-degree right roll and a vertical dive at supersonic speed, causing structural breakup at 10,000 feet. The aircraft crashed into jungle 29 minutes after takeoff with all 47 aboard killed.
probable_cause: Loss of control in flight due to faulty ADI wiring that produced erroneous instrument indications and resulted in inappropriate pilot control inputs. Contributing factors included incomplete training on ADI failure recovery and the design of the ADI switchover system that allowed both displays to be fed by the same faulty instrument.

title: China General Aviation 7552
summary: A newly delivered Yak-42D failed to rotate properly during takeoff at Xiamen. The aircraft lifted off briefly, then slammed back down on the runway. title: Martinair 495
summary: Martinair Flight 495, a DC-10, was attempting to land at Faro Airport in severe weather conditions including a large thunderstorm with heavy rain and low cloud. A faulty thrust-reverser from takeoff was not repaired. Following one unsuccessful landing attempt, the crew attempted another approach through multiple microbursts and windshear. The aircraft made a hard landing with a vertical speed exceeding the manufacturer's design limits. The starboard main landing gear collapsed, the starboard wing separated, the fuel tank ruptured and ignited. The fuselage split in two, resulting in 54 passenger and 2 crew fatalities out of 327 passengers and 13 crew members.
